module purpose: neorv32_spi is a bus-controlled serial transceiver that stores control settings, accepts 9-bit queued transfer items, generates serial clock, chip-select, and data outputs, samples serial input into a receive path, returns control/status or received data on bus reads, and raises an interrupt from FIFO and engine status.

use-case flows.value: controller enable, serial clock mode/rate, and interrupt-enable settings written into ctrl fields
a 9-bit queued transfer item whose tag bit selects chip-select update or serial data transfer
serial transfer state: chip-select selection, serial clock generation, output-bit shifting, input-bit sampling, and completed-byte delivery to the receive FIFO
interrupt request produced from enabled receive, transmit-empty, transmit-below-half, or idle conditions
stored control settings, FIFO and engine status, and received byte returned on bus reads
control, IRQ, transceiver, chip-select, and clock-generator state forced to known values while rstn_i is low
transmit and receive FIFOs cleared while ctrl.enable is low

conceptual assets.reasoning: ctrl.enable is written from bus_req_i.data at line 140 under the bus-write guards at lines 137-139, reset to 0 at line 120, read back at line 153, clears both FIFOs when low (lines 211 and 243), gates irq generation (line 255), is copied into rtx_engine.state(2) (line 281), resets the clock-divider path when low (line 369), and leaves the entity on clkgen_en_o (line 383). Integrity is established because this stored setting decides whether transfers, FIFO retention, interrupt reporting, and external clock-generator enable behave as implemented; availability is established because the bit is held, read back, and exported while not reset. bus_req_i and bus_rsp_o are complete bus transport records, so they are not structural references.

conceptual assets.concept: Serial clock mode and rate settings
conceptual assets.reasoning: ctrl.cpha, ctrl.cpol, ctrl.prsc, ctrl.cdiv, and ctrl.highspeed are written at lines 141-145, reset at lines 121-125, and read back at lines 154-158. cpha and cpol determine rtx_engine.sck assignments at lines 286, 301, 309, 320, 324, and 331; prsc, cdiv, and highspeed determine when spi_clk_en is raised at lines 371-376. Integrity is established because corrupted settings change the serial clock phase, polarity, or rate and therefore the implemented transfer timing; availability is established because these settings are stored and reused across transfers.

ctrl.irq_rx_avail, ctrl.irq_tx_empty, ctrl.irq_tx_nhalf, and ctrl.irq_idle are written at lines 146-149, reset at lines 126-129, read back at lines 164-167, and consumed by the irq condition at lines 255-259. Integrity is established because these stored settings decide which internal conditions are allowed to raise irq_o; availability is established because the settings persist between writes and are read again by the irq generator each cycle.

The queued transfer item re-enters this entity on tx_fifo.rdata from the FIFO subunit (connection at line 207). In state 100, if data is available and the tag bit tx_fifo.rdata(8) is 1, the low four bits are stored in rtx_engine.cs_ctrl at lines 288-290. chip_select then drives all outputs high and asserts one selected active-low bit of spi_csn_o when cs_ctrl(3)=1 at lines 352-355, and line 171 reports the active flag. Integrity is established because external chip selection and the reported active-selection status depend on this stored state; availability is established because the selection is held until another control item or reset or idle clear (lines 275 and 332).

conceptual assets.concept: Serial transmit data byte and outgoing bit stream
conceptual assets.reasoning: The transmit item also re-enters on tx_fifo.rdata from the FIFO subunit (connection at line 207). In state 100, if data is available and the tag bit is not 1, rtx_engine.sreg is loaded from tx_fifo.rdata(7 downto 0) at lines 288-293; later line 318 shifts sreg, and spi_dat_o is driven from sreg(7) at line 343. Integrity is established because the outgoing serial bit stream is defined by this loaded and shifted byte; availability is conditional on queued data and generated clock-enable events. The transport bus write that creates the queue item is excluded from structural references, so tx_fifo.rdata is the eligible local setting point.

spi_dat_i is captured into rtx_engine.sdi_sync at line 310, shifted into rtx_engine.sreg at line 318 while bitcnt advances at line 311, and on the last bit line 321 asserts done. The assembled byte is then presented to the receive FIFO by rx_fifo.wdata <= 0 & rtx_engine.sreg at line 244 with rx_fifo.we <= rtx_engine.done at line 245, and bus reads later return rx_fifo.rdata(7 downto 0) at line 174 through transport-excluded bus_rsp_o. Integrity is established because the received byte that this module stores and hands to its FIFO consumer is defined by these sampled input bits and the completion condition; availability is conditional on a completed transfer.

rtx_engine.sck is the stored serial clock state that is set to ctrl.cpol or toggled from ctrl.cpha and ctrl.cpol at lines 286, 301, 309, 320, 324, and 331, and copied to spi_clk_o at line 344. Those updates occur only when clock_generator raises spi_clk_en using ctrl.enable, clkgen_i or ctrl.highspeed, and cdiv_cnt compared with ctrl.cdiv at lines 369-376. Integrity is established because transfer sampling and shifting and the external receiver both depend on the exact output clock waveform; availability is conditional on enable and the generated clock events.

rtx_engine.busy is computed at line 340 from the low two state bits and therefore represents whether the transfer engine is idle or active. This decision contributes to the reported busy indication at line 172 and to the idle-interrupt qualification at line 259. Integrity is established because incorrect busy or idle classification would violate those implemented report conditions.

irq_o is a registered report that becomes high only when ctrl.enable is set and one enabled source condition is true: rx available, tx empty, tx below half, or idle with no queued data and no engine activity, at lines 255-259; line 253 resets it to 0. Integrity is established because the external interrupt observation depends on this exact Boolean decision; availability is conditional on the enabled source conditions and a clock edge. The separate irq-enable configuration bits are listed as their own stored settings.
